title: IMD Forecasts Heavy Rain, Snow Till Nov 16 as Delhi AQI Eases to Poor
excerpt: A Western Disturbance brings snow to the Western Himalayas till November 13, heavy rain returns to Tamil Nadu and Kerala on November 15-16, and Delhi records a 24-hour average AQI of 299 with no rain forecast till November 15.
body:
• The IMD forecasts scattered to fairly widespread rain and snowfall over the Western Himalayan region till November 13, with isolated heavy rain and snow over the Kashmir Valley on November 12.
  • Isolated heavy rainfall is likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 10-11 and again on November 15-16, and over Kerala and Mahe on November 16, with thunderstorms and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph over Tamil Nadu.
  • Delhi's 24-hour average AQI was recorded at 299 in the 'poor' category on Tuesday, according to The Daily Jagran, while the IMD has predicted no rainfall in Delhi between November 10 and 15.
  • A low-pressure area is expected to form over the Southeast Bay of Bengal around November 13 and become a well-marked low-pressure area within the next 24 hours, according to the IMD via IANS.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast rain and snowfall across the Western Himalayan region till November 13 and heavy rainfall in parts of South Peninsular India through November 16, while Delhi's air quality eased on one widely reported measure even as morning readings stayed higher.

According to IANS reporting of the IMD forecast, a Western Disturbance will bring scattered to fairly widespread rainfall and snowfall over the Western Himalayan region till November 13. Isolated heavy rainfall and snowfall are likely over the Kashmir Valley on November 12. See the IMD advisory.

North: Snow and Rain in the Hills

In Northwest India, isolated to scattered rainfall is likely over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-Baltistan-Muzaffarabad on November 10-11 and 14-16, with fairly widespread to widespread rain and snow during November 12-13, IANS reported. Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand are also expected to receive light to moderate rain at isolated places.

The Daily Jagran, also reporting the IMD update, said the Western Disturbance may bring rain and snowfall to several parts of the Western Himalayan region until November 13, with heavy rain and snowfall possible in some parts of the Kashmir Valley. After snowfall in the mountains, it said, minimum temperatures in Delhi, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh are expected to drop by two to three degrees Celsius over the next two to three days as northwesterly winds reach the plains.

South and Islands: Heavy Rain Windows

In South Peninsular India, isolated to scattered rainfall is forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal from November 10 to 14 and again on November 16, according to IANS. Kerala and Mahe are likely to see rainfall from November 10 to 15, while Lakshadweep may receive rain throughout the week till November 16. Coastal Karnataka, South Interior Karnataka, Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and Rayalaseema are also expected to witness isolated to scattered rain during the latter part of the week.

Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall is predicted over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 15 and over Kerala and Mahe on November 16. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are expected over Tamil Nadu during November 10-12 and 15-16.

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands will see fairly widespread rainfall throughout the week, with isolated heavy rainfall from November 10 to 14, IANS reported. No significant weather is expected over West and Central India during the week, the IMD said.

Delhi: Two Readings, No Rain Expected

Delhi's air quality illustrates why timing matters. The Daily Jagran reported that Delhi's air quality improved slightly on Tuesday, with the 24-hour average Air Quality Index recorded at 299, placing the city in the 'poor' category, just below 'very poor'. A separate IANS report carried by AsiaPOST put Delhi's AQI at 304 around 8:10 a.m. on Tuesday, according to data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), with Pusa and Chandni Chowk recording 395 each.

Both reports agree on the near-term outlook for the capital. The IMD has predicted no rainfall in Delhi between November 10 and 15, and an approaching Western Disturbance influencing the western Himalayan region from Tuesday night is unlikely to bring rain to the national capital. Wind speeds are forecast to remain relatively low, ranging between 5 and 15 kmph in the AsiaPOST report and between 10 and 15 kmph in The Daily Jagran report, limiting dispersion of pollutants. Stage III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) remain in force, AsiaPOST reported.

What to Watch Next

A low-pressure area is expected over the Southeast Bay of Bengal around November 13, becoming well-marked within 24 hours, according to the IMD via IANS. The Daily Jagran said it could bring rain to eastern and southeastern India, while Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and central India stay dry.

For diaspora readers checking home districts: hill districts face snow around November 12-13, Tamil Nadu and Kerala face the heaviest rain around November 15-16, and Delhi faces no forecast rain before November 15.
